extracted.intended_audience: cognitive and affective neuroscientists, psychologists, and researchers studying humor and reward
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing whether a stimulus (e.g., joke, cartoon) qualifies as 'funny' in the strong neural sense by measuring engagement of mesolimbic reward circuitry and related hedonic signatures, and accounting for personality and contextual modulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mesolimbic reward-network activation (NAcc, VTA, amygdala, ACC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Funny stimuli (rated funny by the subject) activate nucleus accumbens, ventral tegmental area (VTA), amygdala, and anterior cingulate cortex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These regions constitute the dopaminergic mesolimbic reward system and associated salience/valuation areas; their activation is the core neural signature that a stimulus is processed as a reward rather than only as understood content. In fMRI studies, look for increased BOLD in these nodes when subjects rate stimuli as funny versus not funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive correlation between BOLD signal and subjective humor intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: BOLD signal in the reward-related regions is positively correlated with subjective humor intensity: the funnier the cartoon/joke is rated, the stronger the activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjective funniness ratings provide a natural, continuous metric that should track neural reward signal strength. Use within-subject correlations or parametric modulation analyses to demonstrate that neural activity scales with reported humor intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus must trigger reward circuitry (not merely comprehension)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a stimulus to count as funny in the strong neural sense, it must trigger reward circuitry rather than only produce cognitive understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish 'clever' stimuli that are understood but do not elicit reward from stimuli that evoke hedonic/motivational responses. An anti-pattern is treating comprehension or appreciation of cleverness as equivalent to humor without evidence of reward-region engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor has a distinct hedonic signature versus other rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: Although humor and monetary rewards both engage the ventral striatum (motivation), humor uniquely engages additional medial prefrontal 'hedonic' regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing reward types, demonstrate both shared motivational circuitry (ventral striatum) and humor-specific medial prefrontal activations to argue that humor is a distinct kind of reward. Use contrast analyses between humor and other reward conditions (e.g., money) to reveal the hedonic signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personality and reward-sensitivity modulate humor-related neural responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual differences such as extraversion predict greater reward-region activity to humor; introversion or reduced reward sensitivity (anhedonia) predict smaller responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for personality/mood variables when evaluating humor responses. Expect variability across participants: extraverts tend to show stronger mesolimbic activation to the same stimuli. Include personality or mood measures as covariates or moderators in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humor functions as reinforcement motivating approach and social-seeking
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor is treated by the brain as a bona fide reward: successful humor comprehension acts as reinforcement, motivating seeking of humor and of the people who provide it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing the behavioral impact of humor, measure approach-related outcomes (e.g., voluntary repetition, preference for the humor source, increased social engagement) in addition to neural activation to demonstrate reinforcement effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude stimuli that produce only other-channel rewards without humor hedonic pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: Stimuli that produce reward only via other channels (e.g., relief, surprise) but do not engage the humor-specific hedonic medial prefrontal pattern should not be classified as humor in the neural sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful attributing neural activation to humor when the effect may instead reflect relief, surprise, or other non-humor rewards. Use pattern/region-specific criteria (e.g., presence/absence of medial prefrontal hedonic activation) to disambiguate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observable engagement indicators as proxy for reward-circuit activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that the audience's reward circuitry is engaged can be visible in laughter, smiles, sustained attention, and voluntary repetition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When neural measures are unavailable, use behavioral/expressive indicators as provisional proxies for reward engagement. However, note these are imperfect and should be interpreted in light of personality and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual diagnostic: audience reward-sensitivity at the moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the audience is reward-sensitive at that moment (extraversion, current mood, absence of anhedonia) affects whether a stimulus will elicit reward responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess situational and trait-level moderators (mood, anhedonia, personality) before concluding about a stimulus's funniness; identical stimuli may produce different neural/behavioral responses across contexts and individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diagnostic check for mismatch between structural prediction and expressed funniness
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare the intensity of expressed funniness to what the joke's structural features would predict; mismatches suggest modulation by reward-evaluation rather than intrinsic joke structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If expressed funniness deviates from structural expectations (e.g., a structurally strong joke rated low), consider reward-sensitivity, mood, or other evaluative modulations as explanations. Use this diagnostic to tease apart structure-driven humor from reward-driven variability.
